text: Vakhtang Tsintsadze - The Asian Development Bank report highlights Georgia’s attractive business environment, as well as ongoing infrastructure projects, including in the port and railway sectors

The Asian Development Bank has published the Asian Economic Outlook report, according to which economic growth in 2025 was quite high at 7.5 percent, while in 2026, amid ongoing conflicts, the Asian Development Bank expects economic growth in Georgia to be 5.5 percent, which is an improvement of 0.5 percentage points compared with the forecast for the previous year,” said Vakhtang Tsintsadze, Deputy Minister of Economy and Sustainable Development.
As the Deputy Minister noted, the Asian Development Bank focuses on reducing the current account deficit to a record low level, as well as on the record-high level of international reserves.
According to Vakhtang Tsintsadze, in 2026 the Asian Development Bank expects the average inflation rate in Georgia to be 3.8 percent, which is a lower figure compared to the previous year.

“The Asian Development Bank also emphasizes that Georgia is striving to become a trade, logistics, and transport hub. In this regard, attention is drawn to a number of reforms that contribute, among other things, to improving customs and other procedures. The bank also highlights the infrastructure achievements that Georgia has made in both the port and railway sectors,” said Vakhtang Tsintsadze.

According to the Deputy Minister of Economy, the ADB report highlights the attractive business environment in Georgia, with attention focused on the free trade agreements that Georgia has, as well as the mechanisms that ensure investor protection, which ultimately increases the confidence and attractiveness of Georgia for both local and international investors.
